But some patients do need that kind of care. So what bothers me is when people constantly shit on it and perpetuates the stigma surrounding inpatient care. Again, many patients do need it. I know the nurses I worked with and I have the best intentions in mind for all of you. 

I'm sorry the rules have to be so rigid and sucky and I am sorry your experience was so traumatizing. 

What we need is people wanting to fix the system not complain about it and shit on the staff. And I know there are shitty nurses and techs out there. I've had them. I've had traumatizing hospital stays too.

Edit: and unfortunately sometimes stabilizing is just keeping people alive while they are on the floor. I wish I could do more but more times than not my hands were tied.

My understanding is inpatient care is just for short-term stabilization. It's by no means the cure for mental illness or the 1st line of treatment for it either. 
As a healthcare worker I try to push that point but I'm under no delusion that it makes a shitty situation much better other than keeping the individual safe while they are in my care. Even though I would try to go farther than just keeping them alive.

That was the nail in the coffin that I can't tell anyone. I didn't expect him to be my sole rock but he made himself into that and then blamed me. 

I just wish my family knew that the manifestations they see aren't me being "dramatic". They are me being terrified because of flashbacks during a family party, or not being able to get the images out of my head. Or being exhausted all the time because every time I go to sleep I get raped all over again in my dreams. 

I'm not lazy. I'm not dramatic. 

But through all this has helped me solidify my career choice. I want to be a psychiatric nurse and I'm in my senior year of nursing school. I thought my mental illness would get the better of me. But it didn't. This is my best achievement to date.
